title: Feed Charge Pump PU-2101B — Mechanical Seal Leakage
immediateAction: Isolate PU-2101B, swap to spare PU-2101A, replace mechanical seal cartridge
problemStatement: Mechanical seal of Feed Charge Pump PU-2101B failed on 12-Mar-2026, causing seal leakage and an unplanned feed reduction to the ARP reactor section.
historicalEvidence: PU-2101B seal MTBF trended down from 26 to 9 months over the last 3 cycles. Seal-flush flow had been intermittently below the 6 L/min design minimum during feed swings, indicating recurring dry-run exposure.
targetCondition: No unplanned feed reduction due to PU-2101B seal failure (seal MTBF ≥ 24 months)

chronology.event: ARP produced resin grade PR-5502 (Reactor Rate ± 13.6 T/H). Field operator noted minor seal weep on PU-2101B during routine round.
Seal flush low-flow alarm annunciated; visible feed seal leak with low suction pressure. Pump auto-tripped on low discharge pressure.
Feed section reduced; charge to reactor curtailed pending seal repair. Rotating team mobilized.
Seal cartridge & shaft sleeve inspected — seal faces heat-checked / worn (dry-running signature).
New seal cartridge installed, pump commissioned, feed restored to ± 13.6 T/H.

fourP.evidence: Operated at 13.1–13.7 T/H vs rated max 18 T/H — within limit.
Suction pressure dropped during feed swing; NPSH margin < 0.5 m (spec ≥ 1.0 m) — cavitation risk.
Seal-flush flow measured 3–4 L/min vs 6 L/min minimum — seal ran dry intermittently.

fourP.parameterOrFactor: Cooling water to seal cooler inadequate
fourP.evidence: Seal cooler outlet temp normal (42 °C) — cooling adequate.
Seal in service 11 months, within 24-month design life.

fourMPlusOneE.parameterOrFactor: No low-NPSH / flush-flow interlock in DCS
fourMPlusOneE.evidence: No automatic trip or alarm on loss of seal-flush flow.

fourMPlusOneE.parameterOrFactor: Feed-swing SOP allows fast rate ramp
fourMPlusOneE.evidence: SOP permits > 2 T/H per minute ramp, driving suction transients.

fourMPlusOneE.parameterOrFactor: PM covers seal only, not flush system
fourMPlusOneE.evidence: Seal-flush plan (Plan 11) not on the PM check-sheet.
Operators trained; no competency gap identified.

verifiedRootCause: Premature mechanical seal failure caused by intermittent dry-running: suction cavitation during feed swings reduced NPSH and seal-flush flow dropped below the 6 L/min minimum, with no interlock to protect the seal.

corrective.action: Install seal-flush flow switch with DCS alarm on PU-2101B
Add low-NPSH / loss-of-flush trip interlock in DCS

proactive.action: Roll out flush-flow switch to PU-2101A spare
Apply interlock standard to all API-682 seal pumps in ARP

preventive.action: Revise feed-swing SOP to cap ramp at 1 T/H per minute
Add seal-flush system (Plan 11) to PU-2101B PM check-sheet

riskOfCorrectiveAction.countermeasure: Stage commissioning with bypass timer & operator brief

pmSchedule.description: Weekly seal-flush flow & seal-pot level check PU-2101B
Quarterly seal condition & shaft run-out inspection

title: Cracked Gas Compressor KO-3201 — High Radial Vibration Trip (Bearing Distress)
immediateAction: Controlled shutdown of compression train, replace DE journal bearing, flush lube-oil system
problemStatement: Cracked Gas Compressor KO-3201 tripped on high-high radial vibration on 29-Apr-2026 due to journal-bearing babbitt distress driven by water-contaminated lube oil.
historicalEvidence: KO-3201 DE vibration baseline is 25–30 micron. Trend shows a steady rise over 5 days preceding the trip. Lube-oil water content had drifted above 500 ppm for ~2 weeks without an online alarm.
targetCondition: No compressor trip due to lube-oil contamination (water < 500 ppm, vibration < 45 micron)

chronology.event: ZCU compression train running normal; KO-3201 drive-end (DE) radial vibration trending up (from 28 to 52 micron over 5 days).
KO-3201 DE vibration reached high-high setpoint (75 micron); machinery protection system tripped the compressor.
Plant rate cut to minimum; lube-oil sample taken — water content 1,800 ppm (spec < 500 ppm).
DE journal bearing removed — babbitt wiped/distressed. Lube-oil cooler tube leak confirmed.
New bearing installed, lube-oil system flushed, cooler tube plugged, train restarted to 55 T/H.

fourP.evidence: DE vibration rose to 75 micron vs 45 micron alarm — bearing distress.
Water content 1,800 ppm vs < 500 ppm spec — film breakdown.
Header pressure 1.8 barg — within normal band.
Bearing in service 3 years vs 6-year design — within life.
Anti-surge margin maintained; no surge event recorded.

fourMPlusOneE.evidence: Water content only checked by weekly grab sample — slow detection.
No routine cooler tube leak check between TAs.
Alert at 60 micron gave little lead time before 75 micron trip.
Purifier available and operational.

verifiedRootCause: Journal-bearing babbitt distress caused by degraded oil-film strength from water ingress via a leaking lube-oil cooler tube, undetected due to absence of online water-in-oil monitoring, leading to rising vibration and a high-high trip.

corrective.action: Repair leaking lube-oil cooler tube (plug + re-test)
Install online water-in-oil sensor on KO-3201 lube system

proactive.action: Retube lube-oil cooler at next TA
Apply online water-in-oil monitoring to KO-3202/3203

preventive.action: Tighten KO-3201 vibration alert to 45 micron & shorten trend-review cadence
Add lube-oil cooler dP & conductivity trend to reliability dashboard

title: Cooling Water Pump PM-4405B (Motor Driven) — Motor Bearing Failure (Overheating)
immediateAction: Start standby CW pump PM-4405C, isolate PM-4405B, replace motor DE & NDE bearings
problemStatement: Cooling Water Pump PM-4405B motor tripped on 08-Jul-2026 due to drive-end bearing failure from grease degradation and an over-extended re-lubrication interval.
historicalEvidence: PM-4405B motor bearing temperature baseline is 60–68 °C. Re-lubrication was performed on a fixed 12-month interval regardless of duty/ambient. Bearing temperature was not trended in CMMS, so degradation went unnoticed.
targetCondition: No motor bearing failure due to lubrication (bearing temp < 75 °C, risk-based re-greasing)

chronology.event: Cooling-water system running on PM-4405B; motor DE bearing temperature trending up (68 → 84 °C).
Motor bearing high-temperature alarm; motor tripped on winding/bearing over-temp.
Standby PM-4405C started; cooling-water supply maintained at reduced margin.
Motor DE bearing found seized; grease degraded/carbonized. NDE bearing marginal.
DE & NDE bearings replaced and re-greased; motor recommissioned.

fourP.evidence: DE bearing reached 84 °C vs 75 °C alarm — grease breakdown.
Running current 132 A vs 150 A rated — within limit.
Fan cowl clean; ambient ventilation adequate.
Correct high-temp lithium-complex grease used.
Bearing in service 2 years vs 5-year design — within life.

fourMPlusOneE.evidence: Fixed 12-month interval too long for duty & ambient — grease degraded.

fourMPlusOneE.parameterOrFactor: Bearing temperature not trended in CMMS
fourMPlusOneE.evidence: No condition-based trigger; only alarm at failure point.
PM-4405B not on the monthly vibration route.
Rounds performed per schedule; local gauge read.

verifiedRootCause: Motor drive-end bearing failure caused by grease degradation from an over-extended, non-risk-based re-lubrication interval, undetected due to absence of bearing-temperature trending, resulting in bearing overheating and motor trip.

corrective.action: Revise PM-4405B re-lubrication interval to risk-based (4-monthly)
Add motor bearing temperature trending & alert to CMMS

proactive.action: Apply risk-based re-greasing to all CW pump motors
Extend bearing-temp trending to utility motor fleet

preventive.action: Add PM-4405B/C to monthly vibration & thermography route
Verify motor cooling-fan & louvre condition each PM

riskOfCorrectiveAction.countermeasure: Use metered re-greasing per bearing volume calc

pmSchedule.description: Monthly motor bearing temperature & vibration reading

title: Feed/Effluent Heat Exchanger HE-3301 — High Fouling — Duty Loss & High dP
immediateAction: Isolate HE-3301, bypass via spare train, hydro-jet clean tube bundle
problemStatement: Feed/Effluent Heat Exchanger HE-3301 suffered accelerated tube-side fouling reducing duty and raising dP, forcing an unplanned isolation, cleaning and partial rate cut on 21-May-2026.
historicalEvidence: HE-3301 tube-side dP baseline is 0.3–0.4 bar; heat duty design 100%. Over the run, dP climbed steadily while duty fell — a classic fouling curve. No dP-based cleaning trigger existed, so fouling was allowed to progress to a forced cut.
targetCondition: No unplanned rate cut due to HE-3301 fouling (dP < 0.6 bar, duty > 90%)

chronology.event: Heat-recovery section running; HE-3301 tube-side dP rising (0.4 → 0.9 bar) and cold-outlet temperature falling.
Preheat duty dropped ~35% below design; unit rate reduced to protect downstream. Exchanger isolated.
Tube bundle inspected — heavy coke/polymer deposition on tube side.
Bundle hydro-jet cleaned and returned to service; duty and dP restored, rate ramped back to 30 T/H.

fourP.evidence: dP reached 0.9 bar vs 0.6 bar limit — heavy fouling.
Duty fell to ~65% of design — loss of preheat.
Heavy-ends 2.4% vs < 1.5% design — increased fouling precursor.
Tube velocity 1.9 m/s vs 1.5 m/s min — adequate.
Shell-side inlet temperature within normal band.

fourMPlusOneE.evidence: Cleaning was time-based only; no dP alarm to trigger action.
Upstream filter dP not monitored, allowing heavy-ends carry-over.
No fouling factor / duty KPI tracked between TAs.
Bundle metallurgy suitable for service.

verifiedRootCause: Accelerated tube-side coke/polymer fouling driven by higher-than-design feed heavy-ends, allowed to progress by the absence of a dP-based cleaning trigger and fouling KPI, causing duty loss, high dP and a forced rate cut.

corrective.action: Add dP-based cleaning trigger & alarm for HE-3301

proactive.action: Apply dP-trigger logic to parallel exchangers HE-3302/3303

preventive.action: Add fouling factor & duty KPI to reliability dashboard
Add upstream filter dP trend & replacement trigger

riskOfCorrectiveAction.countermeasure: Set trigger with hysteresis + engineering review before cleaning

pmSchedule.description: Daily HE-3301 dP & duty trend review
Bundle inspection & cleaning at dP trigger / next TA

title: Product Blower BL-5702 — High Vibration (Coupling Misalignment)
immediateAction: Stop BL-5702, re-align coupling, replace worn coupling element
problemStatement: Product Blower BL-5702 tripped on high vibration on 17-Jun-2026 due to coupling misalignment and a worn coupling element, halting the OPP powder-handling section.
historicalEvidence: BL-5702 vibration baseline is 3.5–4.5 mm/s. A rising trend with dominant 2X harmonic over 2 days indicated developing misalignment. Alignment was last verified 14 months prior; no soft-foot / alignment check in the routine PM.
targetCondition: No blower stop due to misalignment (vibration < 7 mm/s, alignment < 0.05 mm)

chronology.event: OPP running normal; BL-5702 vibration trending up (4.2 → 8.5 mm/s) with 2X harmonic rising.
BL-5702 vibration reached alarm (11 mm/s); blower stopped to prevent damage — powder handling section halted.
Coupling element found worn/cracked; laser alignment showed 0.35 mm offset (spec < 0.05 mm).
Coupling element replaced, unit re-aligned to < 0.05 mm, blower restarted to 38 T/H.

fourP.evidence: Vibration reached 11 mm/s vs 7 mm/s alarm — misalignment signature.
Offset 0.35 mm vs < 0.05 mm spec — angular/parallel misalignment.
Bearing envelope/shock-pulse normal — no bearing defect.
Soft-foot 0.12 mm found on one foot — contributed to misalignment.
1X component within balance grade — no unbalance.

fourMPlusOneE.parameterOrFactor: Alignment check not in routine PM
fourMPlusOneE.evidence: PM did not include periodic laser alignment / soft-foot check.
Elastomer coupling element run beyond recommended 12-month life.
Monthly route missed the fast-rising 2-day trend.
Laser alignment tool & trained technicians available.

verifiedRootCause: High vibration from coupling misalignment aggravated by soft-foot and an over-aged elastomer coupling element, undetected because periodic alignment/soft-foot checks were absent from the PM and the vibration route interval was too long.

corrective.action: Add periodic laser alignment & soft-foot check to BL-5702 PM
Track coupling element life & replace at 12 months

proactive.action: Roll out alignment check to all Class-A blowers in OPP
Create coupling-element replacement register for OPP trains

preventive.action: Shorten BL-5702 vibration route to weekly

riskOfCorrectiveAction.countermeasure: Use wireless vibration sensor for continuous trend
